channel.title: Letters home
channel.description: Moscow, then home: Iyık Janyl under Cathedral Hill

item.title: Twelve years home
item.description: Twelve years since I came home. The walnut gave a lot this year; mama makes the jangak pashtet for the fast days and sells jars to the guests. The season was good. Fewer foreigners than before, more from Talas and Nurzhan. Aigerim's boy is going to Moscow next spring, to the building sites, like…

item.title: A Feast without pilgrims
item.description: This year the Feast was without pilgrims. The quarantine, the checkpoints between the cities, and the archeparchy asked pilgrims to stay at home. Only the people of the city on the hill, standing apart, in masks. Mar Ephrem blessed from the steps to a half-empty square. The bells sounded louder…

item.title: We are on Tulpar now
item.description: Most guests now write to us on Tulpar, the new app. The young ones don't know e-mail. So I check the phone, not the blog. I am a bad blogger now. But I will keep it: this is my Moscow diary, my home diary. Mama asks sometimes to read the old posts. She laughs at "eat soup every day".

item.title: The season is over
item.description: After the Cross (14 September) the pilgrims go home. "After the Cross, no yurt", says the old proverb, and no pilgrims also. This season: 212 nights in our three rooms. Guests from 9 countries. A record. The best: an old woman from Chicago, 84 years, born in Iyık Janyl in 1933, left in 1992 to her…

item.title: Lyudmila Petrovna
item.description: Viktor Ivanovich from Nurzhan, who writes the "Notes of an old refiner", lost his wife. I never met them, but I read his blog for nine years, from Moscow. Today I lit a candle for her in the cathedral, at the icon of St. Janyl. Rest in peace.

item.title: Konok üy Jangak
item.description: We registered the guest house! Patent from the city: three rooms, breakfast only. We painted, new beds from the bazaar, a shower that works (most days). The name is from the old walnut tree in the courtyard: Jangak. First guests: a family from Talas who came for the cathedral, and two Polish…

item.title: The Feast, at home
item.description: For the first time in eight years, the Feast of St. Janyl at home. The night before, the whole hill was candles. The procession from the cathedral, the bells, the icon carried round, the archbishop Mar Ephrem gave the blessing from the steps. Pilgrims from Talas, Nurzhan, from Chicago, from…

item.title: Home
item.description: I am home. Moscow to Tashkent by plane, Tashkent to Namangan in a shared taxi, Namangan to Uchkurgan, then the crossing at Kyzyl-Tuu: three hours in the queue, the Uzbek side, then our side, then a bus to Tash-Kömür and my cousin's car up the river. When I saw the cathedral on the hill from the…

item.title: Irad Day in Moscow
item.description: Irad Day. The Iradi association rented a café in Lyublino, 80 people came, from all over Moscow. The anthem from a phone, everybody stood. Ulak on the TV from the internet, beshbarmak from a lady from Nurzhan, a komuz player who works as a cleaner at the Kazan station and plays like a bird. I…

item.title: Documents
item.description: Today on the metro the police checked my documents again. Third time this month. Our Iradi passport they look at a long time, they don't know it. "Irad? Where is this?" I say: near Kyrgyzstan. "So you are Kyrgyz." No, I am Iradi. "Same thing." Then the registration, the work permit, the stamp, 500…
